contents.text: A modifier is a word or phrase that modifies, or describes, another word or phrase.

header.text: A misplaced modifier is a modifier that appears to modify the wrong word or phrase because it is too far from the word or phrase that it should modify.

sentences.text: Winston saw monkeys and peacocks on vacation in India.
This sentence has a misplaced modifier. It wrongly suggests that the monkeys and peacocks were on vacation.
On vacation in India, Winston saw monkeys and peacocks.
This sentence correctly suggests that Winston was on vacation.

header.text: A dangling modifier is a modifier that appears to modify the wrong word or phrase because the word or phrase that it should modify is missing from the sentence.

sentences.text: Trying to fall asleep, the sheets felt uncomfortably hot.
This sentence has a dangling modifier. It wrongly suggests that the sheets were trying to fall asleep.
Trying to fall asleep, I felt uncomfortably hot in the sheets.
This sentence correctly suggests that I was trying to fall asleep.
